objective: Find an additional full-short-suite improvement beyond LR x2; continue after the completed negative screens.

candidates.single_change: Increase the constant post-warmup learning-rate multiplier from 2 to 2.5.
candidates.hypothesis: LR x2 improves the full suite while LR x3 loses overall; an intermediate rate may retain arithmetic speed without the larger overshoot regressions.

candidates.single_change: Multiply each already normalized attention/FFN branch by the fixed coefficient 1/sqrt(2*layers) before residual addition.
candidates.hypothesis: The embedding-normalized Peri-RMS variant restores coverage but slows recall and small-prime division. A smaller normalized branch may preserve more of the residual signal. This coefficient comes from the inspected transformer architecture, not from long-suite outcomes.
candidates.adaptation: Preserve the exact initial matrices and tied weights; apply scaling after repaired RMS. Do not import the source recipe's projection reinitialization or Schedule-Free optimizer.

screen_policy: Keep original budgets. Require 18/18 passes and improvement in at least three of the six per-task median paired epoch ratios versus LR x2 to advance. Preserve every screen row. No screen-only aggregate geometric mean is reported.
full_suite_policy: Evaluate all 75 paired short cells for every candidate that advances. Prefer complete coverage, then lower full-suite geometric-mean epochs. Compare against both original baseline and LR x2; include all per-task medians/worst cases, slower seeds and censoring. If no candidate improves on LR x2, retain the incumbent and report the negative results.
long_policy: Select only after all advancing candidates have completed 75 short cells. Run a new short winner on the previously observed long regression suite once, without tuning or reselection from long.
invariants: Unchanged frozen model sources, task manifest, data, seeds, batch order, dimensions, dtype, warmup, weight decay, evaluation cadence and update budgets; separately archived code/configuration for every new output directory.
